review_challenges: A backup refusal during legitimate atomic journal mutation is expected safety; require later bounded progress and unchanged old selection rather than treating refusal alone as a defect.
Shared scheduler lock intentionally defers observation; measure and classify contention rather than claiming no lag or exact timer intervals.
Do not remove signer fields or change configuration for unsigned sidecars: preserve same raw configuration with effective per-service secret masks.
Receipt/pending recovery uses one sender lane and original journal; no source/codec relabel, guessed nonce, reset, blind resend or cross-sender adoption.
Do not use accelerated chain time or module-local logical clock as proof of real hourly/multi-day cadence.
Read/source health pins are local file identity, not hardware or remote loaded-code attestation.
Fresh local lock and source group stop are not multi-host signer fencing.
Reuse F6 constructor/snapshot proof under explicit source scope; no construction suite or old component body rerun merely to populate the new lab.
Actual receipt-clearing cycle intentionally skips fresh metadata; second real normal wake is necessary to prove healthy observer recovery, not a rerun of a previously passed test body.
Keep local headers fresh throughout real240-second waits; twelve directed confirmation blocks alone followed by an idle head could cause unrelated valid stale-head refusal.
Derive lab backup capacity from the entire900-second bound and explicit timer interval, including init and intentional partial capture; prior short-fixture32 capacity can exhaust.

Derive shared native log/output budgets from invocation count; repeated full JSON append can exceed64KiB file/capture caps even when each call is bounded. Preserve complete bounded outcome metadata rather than labeling truncated tails complete.
